description: The pie chart visually categorizes “Characters” into two primary groups: “Virtual Characters” and “Real Characters,” with the former occupying the majority of the chart in a large light blue segment and the latter represented by a smaller green segment. Within “Virtual Characters,” six subcategories are displayed in lighter blue shades: “Comic Characters,” “Movie Characters,” “Teleplay Characters,” “Novel Characters,” “Game Characters,” and an unlabeled segment adjacent to “Game Characters,” suggesting a possible seventh category or visual artifact. The “Real Characters” segment is further divided into six subcategories in varying shades of green: “Scientists,” “Artists,” “Athletes,” “Writers,” “Musicians,” and “Influencers,” with “Actors” appearing as a separate, slightly darker green slice adjacent to “Influencers.” The chart uses color coding and spatial arrangement to distinguish between virtual and real character types, with no numerical percentages provided, relying instead on relative slice sizes to convey proportion. The central label “Characters” is overlaid on the chart, with “Virtual Characters” and “Real Characters” labeled directly on their respective segments, emphasizing the hierarchical structure of the classification.
